## View checks by priority

A check is one detail view at one compared stage of one case (the last stage of a shear case left out). Where Response's own view spikes at the stage, Response is unstable there and the check is reported, not assessed: it counts neither inside nor outside (docs/measures.md). A spike: its views at the two neighbouring stages agree with each other within 5 %, and its view at the stage lies more than 5 % from the blend of the two. The other columns are the same checks counted two other ways: with no such rule, and with the rule as first written, which left a check unassessed on the second condition alone, a step as well as a spike.

| Priority | Checks | Inside | Outside | Unstable in Response, not assessed | No rule: inside | No rule: outside | As first written: inside | As first written: outside | As first written: unassessed |

| 3: cracking-related | 1375 | 1345 | 26 | 4 | 1349 | 26 | 1112 | 18 | 245 |

## How the numbers are measured

See `tools/compare.py`. Peak: the largest load on the bottom control chart. Rising and post-peak: the largest distance between the two curves, measured both ways (Response's points from r2c's curve and r2c's from Response's), split at Response's peak; load scaled by Response's peak, control value by its largest value over the whole curve. An r2c point counts as post-peak when its nearest point on Response's curve is at or after Response's peak, so a response that runs on past Response's end, or stops short of it, shows as post-peak distance. Views: at each feature stage of Response's curve (cracking, falls of load, peak, last stage) and r2c's stage at the same place (the nearest in load and control value together, when it is within the target and not across a fall of load; where there is none, r2c's stage at the same feature of its curve), the largest distance of Response's points from r2c's curve, relative to the chart's largest value. For a case with shear the last stage is not assessed and is listed on its own (a last stage that is also the peak is the peak, and is assessed). Unstable: Response's views at the stage before and the stage after each compared stage are blended, line by line and depth by depth, in proportion to where the stage lies between them along the control curve (load scaled by Response's peak, control value by its largest value); Response's own view at the stage is measured against that blend as r2c's is measured against Response's (its departure). The two neighbours' views are measured against each other the same way, each as the reference in turn, the larger of the two taken. Where the neighbours are within the views target of each other and the departure is beyond it (and more than the printed precision), the view spikes there and the check is reported and not assessed. A stage without both neighbours is not tested. Shape: the curve's features in order (cracking, falls of load before the peak, the peak, how the response ends), read alike from both curves; it matches when they are the same. Stage counts are not compared.
